selections.comment: A little bit of a leap of faith may be required to row in behind FEUD, but the likely odds of reward make the well-bred son of Dubawi a tempting proposition. He looked a smart jumping prospect when he scored at the Galway Festival last summer. As it's transpired, he's only appeared once since, when last of those to complete the Grade 3 Grimes Hurdle recently. The positives are that he'll surely come on for that run, Dylan Browne McMonagle has been booked, the stable seems to be returning to form and his mark of 75 seems exploitable. On the back of a chasing success, Dark Note, at the foot of the weights, is a danger to all. Ragmans Corner should make a bold bid to supplement a Navan win.

She confirmed the promise of her point win with a victory on her hurdle debut and likely has more to offer now upped in trip. Derryville went too fast when dropped in distance last time but may do best of the rest here.

selections.comment: SIR CARNEGIE would've placed but for falling last time but can make amends here off an unchanged mark. He's well treated on his maiden form and is a strong traveller so this slight drop in trip with a stiff finish could play to his strengths. Tiny Angel has shown improved form on her last couple of outings and is on a good mark on her UK run so may provide the biggest challenge for a shrewd local yard. Sights Unseen was a C&D winner when last seen in this sphere and with her form franked completes the list of dangers.

selections.comment: An open race where the consistent ZIPSTER gets the verdict. He's proven effective on the AW and turf with his latest run worth marking up significantly as he missed the break leaving him with far too much to do. Harry The Rogue has been equally consistent on a sound surface at around 1m and is entitled to be on the premises once again. Of those at bigger prices Brains makes some small appeal. He isn't the force of old but showed he retained some ability with a 1m in the spring and met trouble last time over an inadequate 7f. He's well treated on his old UK and could gain a place at least here.

selections.comment: DENIM AND DIAMONDS was untested when breaking her maiden on her turf debut dropped in grade and is expected to follow up off a lenient opening mark. She relished the step up in trip that day when never coming off the bridle and likely has more to offer over middle distances. Elana Osario came a long way clear with a classy looking winner on her handicap debut and a 4lb rise looks fair. The drop back in trip won't be an issue and she can continue her progress with her maiden form franked. Sound Of Lightning was a beaten favourite in the Ulster Oaks but she did meet trouble that day and should be competitive here.

selections.comment: This could be fought out by a trio of dual purpose performers. Multiple Graded hurdle winner Zanahiyr was the best of these in that discipline and is unexposed on the flat particularly over staying trips. He's on a generous mark in this sphere so is strongly respected along with veteran Lord Erskine who was a Listed hurdles winner in the spring and will appreciate this step back up in trip. However it may be worth taking a chance with FEUD who has only raced once on the flat for this yard but looked a classy hurdler last summer. He's well treated on that form and is open to improvement now upped to 2m for the first time.

It is the flat bred MONT ST MICHEL who appeals most though taking a significant drop in grade having been used as a pacemaker at Group level last time. He sets a clear standard on ratings and can get the better of Royal Hollow who was Graded placed over hurdles last year and has shown a consistent level of form on the flat from middle to staying trips. The same can be said of Arch Empire who will likely try and make all here and isn't ruled out.
